baseline.name: Track each unit coordinate in a flat array
baseline.approach: Store one flag for every coordinate in range R and update/query each affected cell.
baseline.time: O(w) per width-w range operation; O(R) initialization

archived.name: Lazy segment tree over a fixed node pool
archived.time: O(log R) per contiguous range update/query, where R=10^9 coordinate span; construction initializes a fixed pool of P=400000 nodes
archived.space: O(P) preallocated node pool plus O(log R) recursion depth

why: Assigning coverage to a whole segment avoids visiting every individual coordinate in a large contiguous interval.
quantitative_comparison: The flat model may inspect or write w cells per operation across R=10^9 coordinates. The segment tree follows O(log R) boundary/tree paths; its depth is at most ceil(log2(R))=30. It preallocates P=400000 multi-field nodes rather than R flags, so cell counts are not a byte ratio.
tradeoffs: The node pool has no growth-capacity check and construction allocations are unchecked. Sparse interval-list approaches are other reasonable comparators; this advantage is conditional on the flat-array baseline and valid bounded operations.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
